title: Chyhyryn Raion
summary: Chyhyryn Raion was a district in Cherkasy Oblast, central Ukraine, known for its historical significance during the Ukrainian War of Independence. It was dissolved in 2020 as part of administrative reforms in Ukraine.

sections.heading: Geographical and Administrative Overview
paragraphs: Chyhyryn Raion ([[ukrainian|Ukrainian]]: Чигиринський район) was a district located in [[cherkasy-oblast|Cherkasy Oblast]], in the central part of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. The administrative center of the raion was situated in the town of [[chyhyryn|Chyhyryn]].

sections.heading: Dissolution and Population
paragraphs: On 18 July 2020, Chyhyryn Raion was abolished as part of an administrative reform [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], which aimed to reduce the number of raions in Cherkasy Oblast to four. Following its dissolution, the territory of Chyhyryn Raion was incorporated into [[cherkasy|Cherkasy]] Raion. At the time of its disestablishment, the estimated population of the raion was 25,410.

sections.heading: Hromadas
paragraphs: At the time of its dissolution, Chyhyryn Raion was composed of two hromadas: the Chyhyryn urban hromada, which had its administration in Chyhyryn, and the Medvedivka rural hromada, with its administration located in the selo of Medvedivka.

sections.heading: Historical Significance
paragraphs: The region that encompassed Chyhyryn Raion played a notable role during the [[ukrainian-war-of-independence|Ukrainian War of Independence]], being the site of the Kholodny Yar Republic. This republic, led by local leader Vasyl Chuchupak, existed from 1919 to 1922 and aimed for Ukrainian independence from [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]].
